blocking_defects.description: The policy does not define a canonical immutable GitHub repository identity or exact normalization rules before cross-source comparison.
The policy does not state that missing identity fields never match, so its compound key can behave ambiguously.
Source-range IDs and source priority can change identity assignment when a later source supplies stronger evidence; stable post-normalization candidate identity is not defined.
The policy uses finite 999-record source ranges as the identity mechanism and fails to define stable IDs beyond those ranges.
The exact bug.info grammar, whitelist, malformed-line behavior, unknown-field behavior, duplicate-field behavior, and prohibition on shell evaluation are not defined.

A malformed or incomplete bug definition must be retained as NEEDS_REVIEW, but the candidate schema requires repository and snapshot identifiers; no raw source-record layer exists to account for a non-materializable source object.
Repository URL-to-immutable-GitHub-ID mapping and exact buggy/fix snapshot resolution rules are not defined.
The candidate unit does not define whether same-repository and different-repository package entries expand or collapse into repair episodes.
The exact withdrawn and malware predicates, including malformed values and path-based handling, are not defined.
Accepted GitHub repository, pull-request, and commit URL forms and canonical normalization rules are not fully defined.
Repair-anchor precedence and immutable pre-repair snapshot derivation for commit- and pull-request-linked advisories are not defined.
There is no deterministic per-record disposition for malformed advisories or records lacking materialization fields.
Issue and pull-request search hits do not resolve to one canonical repair episode; issue node IDs can become candidate identities.
Public visibility scope and authenticated-versus-unauthenticated behavior are not fixed.
The search API incomplete_results field is not checked, so a truncated response could be imported.
Issue leads have no deterministic, complete rule for resolving only to merged pull requests.
Required pull-request detail capture and the base.sha candidate snapshot rule are absent.
